symptoms.symptom: Control panel lights go off when you’re setting controls

causes.label: Time too long between touching of selected pads
remedies: Each pad must be touched within 30 seconds of the others.
To relight, touch any pad again, or unlock and relatch door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Time too long between touching of selected pads"

causes.label: Some of the sounds you’ll hear are normal
remedies: Detergent cup opening.
The motor stopping during the drying period.
Water draining out of the tub immediately after you touch START/RESET pad.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Some of the sounds you’ll hear are normal"

causes.label: Utensils are not secure in the rack or something small has dropped into the rack
remedies: Make sure everything is secured in dishwasher.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Utensils are not secure in the rack or something small has dropped into the rack"

causes.label: Motor hums
remedies: Dishwasher has not been used on a regular basis.
If you do not use your dishwasher often, set it to fill and pump out once every week.
This will help keep the seal moist.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Motor hums"

causes.label: Dishes are blocking the detergent cups
remedies: Reposition the dishes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Dishes are blocking the detergent cups"

symptoms.symptom: Water standing in the bottom of the tub

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: A small amount of clean water around the outlet on the tub bottom at the back of the tub keeps the water seal lubricated.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "This is normal"

symptoms.symptom: Water won’t pump out of the tub

causes.label: Drain is clogged
remedies: If you have an air gap, clean it.
Check to see if your kitchen sink is draining well.
If not, you may need a plumber.
If the dishwasher drains into a disposer, run disposer clear.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Drain is clogged"

causes.label: Correct detergent wasn’t used
remedies: Use only automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Cascade®, Cascade Complete® and Electrasol® dishwasher detergents have been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
To remove suds from the tub, open the dishwasher and let suds dissipate.
Add 1 gallon of cold water to the tub.
Close the door until it locks into place.
Pump out water by pressing START/RESET, then after waiting 10 seconds press START/RESET again.
Repeat if necessary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Correct detergent wasn’t used"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Rinse agent was spilled"

causes.label: Detergent with colorant was used
remedies: Some detergents contain colorant (pigment or dyes) that will discolor the tub interior with extended use.
Check the detergent cup for signs of any discoloration.
If cup is discolored, change to detergent without any colorant.
Cascade®, Cascade Complete® and Electrasol® Dishwashing Detergents have been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Detergent with colorant was used"

causes.label: Some tomato-based foods can stain
remedies: Use of the RINSE ONLY cycle after adding the dish to the load can decrease the level of staining.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Some tomato-based foods can stain"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see page 6).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Water pressure is temporarily low
remedies: Turn on a faucet.
Is water coming out more slowly than usual?
If so, wait until pressure is normal before using your dishwasher.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Water pressure is temporarily low"

causes.label: Air gap is clogged
remedies: Clean the air gap.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Air gap is clogged"

causes.label: Improper rack loading
remedies: Make sure large dishware does not block the detergent dispenser or the wash arms.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 11: "Improper rack loading"

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get them clean.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F
remedies: Lower the water heater temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F"

symptoms.symptom: Black or gray marks on dishes

causes.label: Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes
remedies: Remove marks with a mild, abrasive cleaner.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes"

symptoms.symptom: Yellow or brown film on inside surfaces

causes.label: Tea or coffee stains
remedies: Remove the stain by hand, using a solution of 1/2 cup bleach and 3 cups warm water.
CAUTION:               Before cleaning interior wait at least 20 minutes after a cycle for the heating element to cool down.
Failure to do so can result in burns.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Tea or coffee stains"

causes.label: Hard water minerals
remedies: To clean the interior, apply dishwasher detergent to a damp sponge.
Wear rubber gloves.
Do not use any type of cleanser other than dishwasher detergent because it may cause foaming or sudsing.
Cascade®, Cascade Complete® and Electrasol® Automatic Dishwashing Detergents have been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Hard water minerals"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see page 6).
Select HEATED DRY.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser is empty
remedies: Check the rinse agent dispenser.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Rinse agent dispenser is empty"

causes.label: Fuse is blown, or the circuit breaker tripped
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
Remove any other appliances from the circuit.
Try resetting the START/RESET pad.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Fuse is blown, or the circuit breaker tripped"

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: Steam comes through the vent by the door latch during drying and when water is being pumped out.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "This is normal"

symptoms.symptom: Sanitized light does not illuminate at the end of the cycle

causes.label: The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during or after the main wash portion
remedies: Do not interrupt the cycle anytime during or after main wash.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during or after the main wash portion"
